Q: How to find a specific consecutive sequence of rows in SQL without MATCH_RECOGNIZE? A:

In standard SQL this gets a bit clumsier. You'd use LAG and LEAD to access the type in previous and following rows.

One way to write this:

SELECT ts, type, id, district
FROM
(
  SELECT
    ts, type, id, district,
    CASE WHEN (type                            = 'ASSAULT' AND LEAD(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'ROBBERY' AND LEAD(type, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'BATTERY' AND LEAD(ts, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts) BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AND AND LEAD(type, 3) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT')
           OR (LAG(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'ASSAULT' AND type                             = 'ROBBERY' AND LEAD(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'BATTERY' AND LEAD(ts, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts) BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AND AND LEAD(type, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT')
           OR (LAG(type, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'ASSAULT' AND LAG(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  = 'ROBBERY' AND type                             = 'BATTERY' ts                                 BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AND AND LEAD(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT')
           OR (LAG(type, 3) OVER (ORDER BY ts) = 'ASSAULT' AND LAG(type, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  = 'ROBBERY' AND LAG(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  = 'BATTERY' AND LAG(ts, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AND type                             = 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT')
    THEN 1 END AS keep_this
  FROM crimes
) c
WHERE keep_this = 1
ORDER BY ts;

Another way:

SELECT ts, type, id, district
FROM
(
  SELECT 
    ts, type, id, district,
    LAG(type, 3) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  AS t1,
    LAG(type, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  AS t2,
    LAG(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  AS t3,
    type                             AS t4,
    LEAD(type, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS t5,
    LEAD(type, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS t6,
    LEAD(type, 3) OVER (ORDER BY ts) AS t7,
    LAG(ts, 2) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AS ts2match,
    LAG(ts, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts)  BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AS ts3match,
    ts                             BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AS ts4match,
    LEAD(ts, 1) OVER (ORDER BY ts) BETWEEN 1755864000 AND 1755873000 AS ts5match
  FROM crimes
) c
WHERE ('ASSAULT', 'ROBBERY', 'BATTERY', 'MOTOR_VEHICLE_THEFT', TRUE) IN
(
  (t1, t2, t3, t4, ts2match),
  (t2, t3, t4, t5, ts3match),
  (t3, t4, t5, t6, ts4match),
  (t4, t5, t6, t7, ts5match)
)
ORDER BY ts;

Maybe there is still a more elegant way to write this, but I cannot think of any at this moment.

Q: Reload certs without restart of server kestrel A:

One update if you're reading this in 2026. If the reason you reload is Let's Encrypt renewal, the cadence now matters more: Let's Encrypt issues 6-day certificates and is taking the default lifetime down to 45 days, so you renew far more often and a fixed schedule stops being safe. The CA hands you a renewal window through ACME Renewal Information (RFC 9773) that you're meant to follow.

I handle both parts, the selector swap and RFC 9773 renewal, in a library called AutoHttps (disclosure: I'm the author): https://github.com/astralmaster/AutoHttps . If you only need the reload and issue certificates elsewhere, the selector callback in the other answers is all you need.

Q: Why does the assignment of Font object fail? A:

To make the assignments work, I had to create separate assignments for each Font property.

That's how you set fonts on a Range, because the Range.Font has no setter, so you can't Set it directly.

The weird errors are because VBA is trying very hard to make the assignment work as written, through a mechanism that attempts to invoke the object's default member at run-time: since Range.Font is get-only, it's being interpreted as Set RNG.Font.[_Default] = SomeFont, but the default member of Font is most likely its Name (a String), and the assignment is thus a type mismatch error.

Side note, Rubberduck (free & open-source VBE add-in I maintain) inspections would have warned about this.

Q: Compatibility of JDBC driver with Oracle 19c Database A:

You can use the JDBC versions below as per your requirement.

These are the .jar files for different versions of Oracle:

  • ojdbc14.jar ----- Oracle 10g
  • ojdbc6.jar ----- Oracle 11g
  • ojdbc7.jar ----- Oracle 12c
  • ojdbc8.jar ----- Oracle 19c
